title: ModuleNotFoundError
kicker: Python for SDFs · Fix the error

notes.label: ModuleNotFoundError
notes.text: The type of error. Python looked for a library called fitz and it isn't installed in this Colab session.

notes.label: No module named 'fitz'
notes.text: The name from your import line. `fitz` is the import name of PyMuPDF, a PDF library that Colab doesn't come with.

notes.label: In Colab
notes.text: Below this error, Colab also prints a NOTE that suggests installing with `!pip`. That's Colab's hint for exactly this case.

fixes.label: !pip install pymupdf   (in a cell above; run it first)
fixes.title: Best fix
fixes.feedback: The install cell downloads PyMuPDF into this Colab session, and then `import fitz` works. A new runtime starts without it, so keep the install cell at the top and run it each time you connect.
fixes.fixed_code:
# Test fixture, not shown to students: stands in for running `!pip install pymupdf` in a cell above, which Pyodide can't do.
import sys, types
sys.modules["fitz"] = types.SimpleNamespace(open=lambda path: types.SimpleNamespace(page_count=3))
# The fixed cell, after the install cell has run:
import fitz
doc = fitz.open("/content/sample-sdf-document.pdf")
print(doc.page_count)

fixes.label: !pip install fitz
fixes.title: Wrong library
fixes.feedback: PyPI has an unrelated, unmaintained package called fitz. Installing it doesn't give you PyMuPDF, and PyMuPDF's docs warn against it. Install pymupdf. `fitz` is only the name you import.
fixes.fixed_code:
!pip install fitz
import fitz
doc = fitz.open("/content/sample-sdf-document.pdf")
print(doc.page_count)

fixes.label: import pymupdf
fixes.title: Still a ModuleNotFoundError
fixes.feedback: Recent PyMuPDF versions can be imported as pymupdf too, but only after the library is installed. Changing the name doesn't install anything, and line 2 still uses fitz.

links.label: PyMuPDF docs: installation, and the fitz name

learn.used_later: Project 3's notebooks open with `!pip install pymupdf`, and the notebooks in Projects 7 and 8 start with their own install cells. When an import fails, check that the install cell ran in this session.
